content.comment_body: I have several [product_name] devices overseas and things worked well: whenever they needed a new program, I simply created it and sent it on a [product_name] memory card. Now, I only have two local devices, but they don't accept the old memory card. I moved the program to a newer model memory card—will they be able to download it from this? What solutions are available?
Hello [user_name], please check this link: [url]. I hope you find it helpful.

Thank you for your help. This clarifies compatibility, but doesn't solve my current issue. As I see it, I'll need to replace all our [product_name] devices with newer models to maintain our workflow; then I could remotely program and send out memory cards from the UK. Would [company_name] want me to do this, or will they repeat such changes again and force me to upgrade hardware repeatedly? If anyone knows where to obtain yellow memory cards and [article_no], I'd be interested.
Hi, why not obtain an older type as a backup for servicing your existing older units?

Hi [user_name], I considered that, but I'd still need a stock of yellow memory cards. Red cards aren't suitable since we'd need one for each [product_name] device; with a yellow card, I can program an entire production line. I truly believe [company_name] should offer better support for their legacy products.
If you require an older version of [product_name], I can arrange it if needed.
Thanks. Am I understanding correctly—you can supply some of the old yellow memory cards?
Yes! Please provide input/output and power supply details to help select a compatible unit.

Thank you, [user_name]. Right now, I only want around six old yellow memory cards with [article_no]. We already have the [product_name] devices, but without available memory cards, they're becoming unusable. Regards, [user_name]
Sorry [user_name], currently I have some old and new series of [product_name], and four memory cards of [article_no]. Thanks, [user_name].
Hi! I have three yellow and four red memory cards. If you're interested, please send me a private message.
Thank you, [user_name]. I have sent a private message.

Hello [user_name], if [company_name] replaces a product with a newer version, it's usually still possible to order the older one for some time, though eventually only as a spare part. Contact your [company_name] office to ask if your [product_name] or yellow card is available as a spare part. Another approach: when all your devices are upgraded, what happens to the yellow card? Ask your operator to return it for reuse. [company_name] offers a [product_name] PROM unit that can duplicate cards, with copies created from a master device or card. Hope this helps.

Thanks, [user_name]. I'm now checking with my supplier. Unfortunately, a PROM unit isn't helpful, as we have too many program variations and prefer keeping each program on its own card. When the product line changes, supervisors can easily update each device using individual cards. Since the production line is in China and I'm in the UK, sending specific cards has been the simplest way for updates. We don't want the local team having the software to prevent unauthorized modifications. Thanks again—hopefully my supplier can source some.
Hi! I came across some automation equipment on Ebay.co.uk. Is this the type of memory card you're seeking? [url]
Yes, that's exactly what I need. Thanks a lot. Based on [user_name]'s advice, I'm now trying to obtain some from my supplier, and it seems promising.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are facing ongoing compatibility challenges between legacy and newer memory modules for [product_name] devices, disrupting efficient remote programming practices. The lack of backward compatibility and limited availability of older modules are causing workflow disruptions and operational risks. Users are frustrated by the lack of long-term support and backward compatibility, expressing concerns regarding [company_name]'s support for outdated but still deployed hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect either backward compatibility between memory modules throughout different [product_name] generations, or continued availability of legacy memory cards. They wish to maintain remote programming capabilities without having to replace hardware, and seek long-term support for earlier hardware versions.
